items.title: AP News Summary at 6:11 p.m. EST | Associated Press National | nvdaily.com
items.excerpt: Parts of the US clean up, power being restored after Thanksgiving storm soaks East Coast Heavy rain over the East Coast is winding down, with power slowly being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers. The storms led to travel disruptions, downed trees and water rescues from New York to Virginia. Wet snow was falling as far south as the Tennessee Valley, while freezing rain moved across northern New England. Another storm system in the Northwest brought rain to coastal Oregon. More snow was forecast in the Cascades and mountain passes in Montana and Wyoming. Conditions are expected to improve in the eastern U.S., but the system will take time to weaken. US military says it disabled another ship that tried to breach naval blockade on Iranian ports WASHINGTON (AP) — The US military says it disabled another ship in the Gulf of Oman that tried to breach naval blockade on Iranian ports. U.S. Central Command said Friday the military disabled the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday by firing “precision munitions” at the ship’s stern from a military aircraft. It said, “The ship’s propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed." The Pacific Archer is at least the 15th disclosed vessel to be disabled by the U.S. military since the blockade began in the spring and the sixth since it resumed this summer. The previous vessel was disabled on Nov. 7. AP Exclusive: Lebanon's prime minister says a proposal is underway to have UN peacekeepers stay on BEIRUT (AP) — Lebanon’s prime minister says a new proposal could allow the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon to continue after its mandate expires at the end of the year. Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told The Associated Press in an exclusive interview on Friday that France is preparing a resolution to extend some of UNIFIL's functions, like clearing mines and escorting humanitarian convoys. U.S. officials have indicated openness to this arrangement. The U.N. Security Council voted last year to end UNIFIL’s mandate by 2026. The Lebanese government is negotiating with Israel on troop withdrawal and Hezbollah disarmament, but talks are stalled amid regional tensions. Zelenskyy urges US to pressure Putin and questions Trump's reference to Putin as a 'friend' KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed frustration with the U.S. approach to Russian leader Vladimir Putin. He wants American officials to put more pressure on Putin to stop the invasion of Ukraine, which began almost five years ago. Zelenskyy said Friday that he finds it strange that U.S. President Donald Trump called Putin a friend at a recent summit. The International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Putin for war crimes. Meanwhile, European Union leaders failed to reach consensus on a new $49 billion loan for Ukraine. Elections in the EU could affect support for Ukraine as the war continues. Pakistan and Turkey pledge to support Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks under defense pact ISLAMABAD (AP) — Pakistan and Turkey have pledged support for Saudi Arabia against Houthi rebel attacks. The three nations held talks Friday under a trilateral defense pact that treats an attack on one member as an attack on all. Pakistani officials said defense and military leaders met in Islamabad to discuss Middle East developments and back diplomatic efforts to ease tensions. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said the nations condemned attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. Turkey and Pakistan describe the agreement as purely defensive. Turkish officials said Ankara might send military assistance to Saudi Arabia but no troops would be deployed. Stocks jump to close out an erratic week that was also Wall Street's best in more than a year NEW YORK (AP) — Stocks jumped and nudged Wall Street to its best week in more than a year following several days of erratic swings for influential technology companies. The S&P 500 index rose 1.6% Friday. The benchmark index notched a 5.6% gain for the week, its biggest since April of 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 591 points, or 1.2%. The Nasdaq composite rose 2.3%. The strong finish caps an otherwise unsteady week for markets. Stocks opened with a rally on Monday, then swung sharply on Tuesday and Wednesday. Markets were closed in the U.S. on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027. The sharp upward revision to gross domestic product last quarter, reported by the Commerce Department on Wednesday, marked the quickest economic growth pace in three years. It reflected upgrades to consumer spending and business investment, mostly related to artificial intelligence. Robust domestic demand is fueling inflation, with a measure of underlying price pressures in October posting its biggest year-over-year increase since late 2023. The economy has powered ahead despite the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. "It is more urgent than ever that Fed officials step up the pace of interest rate hikes to cool off economic demand," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "It was once thought that import tariffs and energy prices from the Mideast war were one-off factors behind the higher inflation numbers, but increasingly the inflation fires look to be stoked by old-fashioned economic demand pressures." GDP increased at a 4.3% annualized rate last quarter, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis said in its second estimate of third-quarter GDP. It was the fastest pace since the third quarter of 2023. The ... Growth in consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the economy, was revised up to a 4.2% rate. That was the strongest pace since the fourth quarter of 2024 and was an upgrade from the previously reported 3.8% pace. Spending is being driven mostly by higher-income households, whose wealth was boosted by the stock market before the ongoing AI-led selloff. Economists expect consumer spending to slow to a still-healthy pace in the fourth quarter, though declining gasoline prices should ease some of the financial pressure on middle- and lower-income households. ... The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index increased 0.3% in October after gaining 0.5% in September, the BEA said. PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. In the 12 months through October, PCE inflation increased 3.8% after advancing 3.6% in September. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the PCE Price Index increased 0.3% for the third straight month. So-called core PCE inflation increased 3.3% on a year-over-year basis in October, the largest advance since November 2023, after climbing 3.1% in September.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate.

items.title: ‘Focker In-Law,’ ‘The Hunting Wives,’ and audio erotica top this week’s Must List
items.excerpt: ## *Focker In-Law* ... Greg Focker (Ben Stiller) is back to cause chaos. But this time, the shoe is on the other foot — as he bristles against his son Henry’s (Skyler Gisondo) new girlfriend, Olivia (Ariana Grande). And while *Focker In-Law* does a great job of ushering in the new generation of Fockers, it wouldn’t be a *Meet the Parents* film if Jack Byrnes (Robert De Niro) wasn’t a thorn in Greg’s side too. *Focker In-Law*, a return to form for the franchise, is full of nostalgic Easter eggs and new dynamics that will surely please fans of the original 2000 film. — *Daysia Tolentino, News Writer* ## *The Hunting Wives* season 2 ... Season 2 of the Netflix series goes off-book — and off the rails. With no more source material left to adapt, the story expands with a lot more wigs, guns, lesbian sexual experiences, an in-world Bravo-esque reality show, and murder. So *much* murder that the showrunner dubs them “Murder Wives” instead. — *Nick Romano, Senior Editor* ## Nina Dobrev and Paul Wesley’s Quinn Original *The Haunting of Pendle Creek* ... *Vampire Diaries* fans can sink their teeth into the former costars’ NSFW audio erotica series, following two exes as they investigate mysterious disappearances in a haunted town. It’s a nostalgic reunion, only this time without the CW’s teen-oriented guardrails. The verdict? Sorry, Damon, Stelena’s chemistry is still *scorching*. — * Kat Pettibone, Senior Editor* ... Looking for a way to fill the gap between the just-completed *Traitors: New Blood* ... Head over to NYC’s St. Luke’s Theatre for a hilariously absurd musical tribute featuring faithful (get it?) impressions of Britney Spears, Liza Minnelli, Jennifer Coolidge, and… Jesus Christ?

items.title: AP Entertainment SummaryBrief at 5:01 p.m. EST | Features | rutlandherald.com
items.excerpt: Peter Gabriel on his full moon albums, the future of AI and the end of Genesis LONDON (AP) — Peter Gabriel released the inventive art rock album “o\i” on Friday. It is a companion piece to 2023's “i/o,” transforming the collection into 25 tracks. Gabriel shared his thoughts in a London-based interview with The Associated Press' Hilary Fox. He discussed the symbolism of full moons, artificial intelligence's impact and the role of activism in music. He believes AI can democratize creativity but acknowledges it could lead to job losses. Gabriel also touched on the importance of speaking out for causes and reflected on his time with Genesis. He attended their final show in London, finding it an emotional and significant moment. Princess Kate takes to the mountains to face mortality in film about cancer recovery LONDON (AP) — Princess Catherine shares her journey of cancer diagnosis and recovery in a new documentary called "Heal." The film follows her as she takes on the Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland, and Wales. She reflects on the importance of having someone by her side during her darkest times. The documentary highlights her gratitude for medical treatment and the realization that life is short. Proceeds from the film will support the Royal Marsden hospital. Catherine emphasizes holistic healing, balancing effort and acceptance, and the power of vulnerability in connecting with others.

items.excerpt: As Tsatsamis, the Greek-British musician has had a banner year, opening for Adéla and Jessie Ware off the back of his remarkable mix tape, Tsycophant. Like them, he is a live-wire performer who favours fast-paced dance music and club catharsis to the therapist’s couch. Fusing George Michael’s stage presence with Sophie’s tactile beats, Tsatsamis not only has the production chops to make floor-filling anthems and the pipes to blast them to the rafters, but the emotional acuity to unpack his vulnerability without unravelling in the process. Consider his latest single, Masochist. ... ​ Molly Santana – Sailin’ On The California rapper had a huge breakout this year via Drake’s Ran to Atlanta, and she now drops noisy debut album Black Punk. Sailin’ On certainly proves her punk bona fides, quoting Bad Brains’ Pay to Cum and splicing trap with hardcore riffs.
